methodological_rigor.justification: Machine learning study with appropriate cross-validation (5-fold repeated) to mitigate overfitting. Five algorithms compared (XGBoost optimal). SHAP analysis for feature interpretability. Reasonable sample size (n=584). Appropriate model evaluation metrics (AUC). Train-test performance reported (0.868 vs 0.764) suggesting reasonable generalization.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preoperative predictive model for STAS in NSCLC. Direct clinical relevance to surgical planning and prognostication. However, validation limited to single center. Real-world clinical utility requires prospective external validation.

reporting_quality.justification: ML methodology clearly described. Cross-validation and feature importance (SHAP) appropriately reported. However, missing external validation cohort and no explicit data availability statement for model/data sharing.

novelty_literature.justification: STAS prediction modeling extends existing knowledge of this pathologic feature. XGBoost approach to radiomics interpretation offers methodological contribution. Clinically meaningful but methodologically incremental.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear presentation of ML methodology and results. SHAP analysis well-explained. Some sections could benefit from more clinical context.

key_strengths: Rigorous ML methodology with repeated 5-fold cross-validation
SHAP analysis provides interpretability of model predictions
Clinically actionable decision-support tool for preoperative planning
key_concerns: Train-test performance gap (0.868→0.764) suggests potential overfitting despite cross-validation
Limited discussion of clinical implementation challenges (cost, accessibility of CT semantic analysis)
No comparison to simpler clinical/radiologic scoring systems
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-designed ML study with solid methodology and clinical relevance. Tier 3 pending external validation and prospective clinical impact assessment.
